notes: app 1.11.3 + chart 0.10.0. App: the appliance was three minor versions behind, and 1.8.22 predates per-request origins (APPLIANCE_ORIGINS) — a published box keeps its LAN names and a browser must be told to load OnlyOffice and LiveKit from the name it arrived on. Chart: onlyoffice/livekit ingresses gain extraHosts, so one Ingress can carry a second name with its own TLS secret. Both are iso-behaviour on a box that is NOT published: with no LAN names the rendered objects are byte-identical (checked against a golden render), and extraHosts is empty. app_version drives the app/sandbox/workbench image pins in values.yaml (the appliance pins them for offline safety, update.sh rewrites all four on apply); the four images are built under one version by suite-366's Publish Public Image workflow. Bump chart_version / app_version / vllm_image here to roll out to the fleet; appliances poll this file daily and notify (no auto-apply), and since the strictly-newer comparison landed a channel BEHIND a box is reported rather than offered. updater_sha256 and backup_sha256 are filled in by tools/sign-channel.sh - never by hand; they are what let an appliance trust the update.sh and backup.sh it fetches. restic_version and the two restic_sha256_* fields are pinned from lib/config.sh by the same script, so an appliance that grows a backup agent online can also fetch the binary that runs it - and verify it against a hash we signed rather than against whatever GitHub serves. backup_sha256 must be present: an appliance holding the package key REFUSES to refresh backup.sh without it, and a box whose updater rolls forward while its backup agent does not is a box that silently stops being backed up.
